findings.title: The ARM1_SENSE-to-CAM_IO_3V3 bridge figures (about 1.73 V on RAW_ACT, about 0.15 mA through the match) omit the D120 / R131 cold pull-up, which is live whenever CAM_IO_3V3 is; the board-on values are about 2.19-2.21 V and 0.107-0.109 mA
findings.contradicts: docs/R10_VALIDATION.md line 2603 (section 1, surface inventory): 'ARM1_SENSE ... to U13.5 (CAM_IO_3V3), benign: at most 3.3 V on PC5 and about 1.73 V on RAW_ACT with the bus off, about 0.15 mA through the match against the J-Tek 0.30 A no-fire, and the cold screen then reads the bus as live and refuses (Calculation; ...)'. The source derivation (round22_safety.json, consequences_calculation) is '3.3 V x 11.2/(10.2+11.2) = 1.73 V', a divider of R132 + R175 (10.2 kOhm) against the CONT bank (11.2 kOhm) only.
findings.evidence: Board a0ec075e (pcbnew 10.0.7, read-only): CAM_IO_3V3 is U13 (TPS70933) pin 5, fed only from CAM_5V (U402 TPS2553, EN = CAM_PWR_EN = PE11 with R431 100 kOhm pull-down; U402 IN = PORT_5V3, off on USB-only power and with J400 open). So CAM_IO_3V3 is at 3.3 V only while the board runs, i.e. while 3V3 is up. The cold pull-up D120 (BAT54A, pin 3 = 3V3 anode, pin 1 = PYRO1_COLD) -> R131 10 kOhm (B(10.8,61.15)) -> PYRO1_OUT is then live. Nodal solve (.supervisor/r30_safety/camio_bridge.py, output camio_bridge.txt; ARM1_SENSE stiff at 3.3 V, R132 + R175 = 10.2 kOhm into RAW_ACT, R134 2 Ohm, match 2 Ohm, CONT bank 11.2 kOhm, Q120/Q121/Q124 off): without the pull-up RAW_ACT = 1.7274 V and I_match = 0.1542 mA (the record's figures, reproduced exactly); with it, Vf 0.20 / 0.24 V (JSCJ BAT54 VF1 <= 0.24 V at 0.1 mA, cached r14_parts_pdf/bat54.pdf p1): RAW_ACT = 2.2052 / 2.1913 V, I_match = 0.1073 / 0.1087 mA, CONT = 196.9 / 195.6 mV. The sentence's own condition ('the cold screen then reads ...') is the board-on state. Only with 3V3 off (a camera back-feeding J9.1 with the board off, which REQUIREMENTS F9 forbids) do 1.73 V / 0.154 mA apply.
findings.impact: A wrong safety-record value (27 % low on RAW_ACT). The conclusion is unchanged: about 0.11 mA is far below the 0.30 A no-fire, and PC5 reads 3.3 V, so the cold screen refuses.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only, R10_VALIDATION section 1: 'at most 3.3 V on PC5 and, with the board on (3V3 feeding the D120 / R131 cold pull-up), about 2.2 V on RAW_ACT with the bus off and about 0.11 mA through the match (0.15 mA and 1.73 V only with 3V3 off, a back-fed camera, which the procedure forbids) ...; Calculation / Inference: the BAT54 drop at 0.1 mA'.

findings.title: The first-article 70 C chamber test cannot pass as written: its new criterion 'LS120 <= 70 C' in a 70 C chamber at the pad load is physically unattainable (the docs themselves put LS120 at 80-92 C there), so the 55 C interim site limit could never be lifted and none of the listed failure remedies addresses LS120
findings.contradicts: Kind 3 (a required procedure cannot be carried out correctly as written; documents contradict). REQUIREMENTS Temperature row: 'Until the first-article 70 C chamber test at the pad load passes (every 85 C part <= 85 C, and LS120 <= 70 C (thermocouple on LS120); ORDERING 8.3), the interim site limit is bay air <= 55 C'; the same criterion in ORDERING 8.3 'Board temperature at the pad load' ('Pass: every 85 C-rated part <= 85 C, and LS120 <= 70 C'), M3_R10 'Hot-end temperature', R10_VALIDATION owner rows 33 and 36 ('pass: LS120 <= 70 C'), parts_qualification 'Round 29'. The same sentences state that at the pad load LS120 'runs at about 80-92 C in a 70 C bay' (+10-22 K, Inference), and owner row 36 accepts buzzer annunciation as best-effort above about 48 C bay air.
findings.evidence: In a 70 C chamber with the board dissipating the pad load (1.0-1.5 W) and no cooler boundary, every board-mounted part is above 70 C in steady state (all heat sources are on the board; LS120 at F(23,58.5) is soldered to it). The docs' own model gives LS120 80-92 C there (70 + 10..22 K). So the LS120 clause fails on every board, and with it the whole chamber test; the listed failure remedies ('a camera / port duty limit on the pad, or X7R parts on the same lands', REQUIREMENTS / M3_R10 / owner row 33) do not lower LS120's pad-load rise, so the 'until it passes' 55 C limit becomes permanent, while owner row 36 treats LS120's out-of-rating state as accepted and non-gating. Introduced by the round 29 fix pass (R29-TRI-04).
findings.impact: The thermal acceptance gate for the 85 C parts can never be closed on this board, so the interim limit and the owner's 48 C best-effort disposition contradict each other; procedure unusable as written. No fire hazard; the buzzer is annunciation only (the stay-off checks also use telemetry).
findings.concrete_fix: Text only, in the six places: drop LS120 from the pass criterion (its hot end is owner row 36's accepted best-effort item) and instead 'record LS120's rise over chamber air at the pad load (thermocouple on LS120); the buzzer stays in rating for bay air <= 70 C minus that rise, which replaces the inferred 48 C'. Keep 'every 85 C part <= 85 C' as the pass criterion.

observations: BAT_ENABLE to BAT_OVLO 0.200 mm (U9.1 to U9.2, B.Cu, TI land) is not in the section 1 table; fail-safe: J400 open, EN sits at about 0.57 V (OVLO divider 2 MOhm / 280 kOhm loaded by R81); J400 closed, OVLO rises to about 1.55 V and trips U9 off.

ACT_GATE to BAT_IN 0.2177 mm (B.Cu, the Q120 gate chamfer (14.475,72.2)-(15.262,72.987) to Q120.9) is not listed; a bridge holds the P-FET pair off (no inadvertent bus), and loss of the bus is caught by rule 4's powered-BUS refusal.

PYRO1_OUT to BUZZ_G 0.510 mm (R173.1 to the BUZZ_G track (17.92,58.70)-(17.75,58.87), B.Cu) is outside the section 1 rows; identical (0.510 mm) on 92c3ad59, so not a D-R26 change; R162 1 kOhm and R163 10 kOhm limit an enabled bus to about 10 mA: no fire.

U9.1-U9.5 row 'leak of at most 1.52-1.83 MOhm' spans both pack voltage and VUVLO(R) spread (1.83 uses 1.183 V at 8.4 V; the max-threshold bound at 8.4 V is 1.76 MOhm), while the RAW_ACT latch row uses the worst threshold at both ends (1.69-1.96 MOhm); inconsistent convention, ambiguous 'at most', not counted.
R134 '22-29 W' for a PYRO1_IGN-to-GND short: 3.3-3.75 A gives 21.8-28.1 W at 2 Ohm (28.4 W with hot R134 min); the 29 W top is a loose upper bound, conclusion unchanged.
The J440.3-chafe EN figure 1.28 V is right once the 1 kOhm TX series resistor is counted (3.3 x 300 / 771 = 1.284 V).

Rule 4 probe points match the copper: R120 and C120 sit on Q120's own B.Cu gate island (Q120.4-(15.262,72.987)-via (16.2,73.3)-C120.2-R120.2), R119 on Q121's; so a Q120 gate cut from R121 reads about 0 V at R120.2 against R120.1 (ACT_FET_S).
Rule 3 meter check: U3.3 is QSPI_IO2 and QSPI_IO2 has no pull-up, so the red-on-R127.1 path is GND clamp + 0.91 kOhm as stated (1 k || 10.22 k = 0.9109 kOhm).

Single-fault sweep with J400 open: ACT_GATE to GND / RAW_ACT (Q121.4-Q121.9 0.520 mm) / any low node, ACT_DRV to GND, Q122 or Q121 D-S short energise the bus without firing (Q124 held by R128, MCU off) and are screened by per-flight step 2 (J121.2 < 0.1 V) and owner row 2; EN-node paths (U9.1-U9.5, the (17.1,82.8) via-BAT_FAULT_N, ACT_EN / ACT_EN_MCU / RAW_ACT to BAT_ENABLE) are owner row 24 and steps 2/3. No single fault found that fires, or turns the board on with J400 open, outside the records.

AGENTS section 2.4 holds on the board: Q124 R126 220 Ohm series / R128 10 kOhm to source / C126 220 nF gate-source (source = GND); Q122 R122 / R123 / C123; Q120/Q121 R121 series, R119 / R120 to ACT_FET_S, C120 gate-source; PE4 also has R127 1 kOhm at the pin (gate <= 0.104 V against a 30 kOhm pull-up at 3.6 V).
